- **Web boundary:** Spring MVC prepares the model before both visit endpoints: it loads the owner/pet, constructs a new `Visit`, and attaches it to the pet. The POST handler validates the bound visit and directly calls `VisitScheduler.bookVisit(...)`; validation failures return to the form instead. (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/ui/VisitController.java:67-84`, `:89-105`)
- **Direct application/domain calls:** `bookVisit` reloads the managed owner, directly calls `Owner.addVisit`, then flushes the owner repository. `Owner.addVisit` resolves the pet and directly delegates to `Pet.addVisit`, which adds the visit to its JPA collection. (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/application/VisitScheduler.java:44-49`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/domain/Owner.java:174-189`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/domain/Pet.java:68-71`, `:89-95`)
- **Persistence:** `Pet.visits` is a cascading `@OneToMany` joined by `pet_id`; therefore flushing the managed owner aggregate inserts the new `Visit`. `Visit` maps to `visits` and receives its ID through `IDENTITY`, which is why the event can contain `visit.getId()` after the flush. (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/domain/Pet.java:68-71`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/domain/Visit.java:37-47`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/application/VisitScheduler.java:46-49`)
- **Event delivery, not a direct cross-module call:** after persistence, `VisitScheduler` publishes the public `VisitBooked(visitId, petId, date)` event. (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/application/VisitScheduler.java:27-30`, `:48-49`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitBooked.java:20-25`)
- **Cross-module reaction:** Spring Modulith delivers that event to the vet module’s `@ApplicationModuleListener`; the listener then directly calls `VetRoster.assignVet`. The roster selects the least-loaded vet and persists a new visit assignment. Thus owner→vet is event delivery, while listener→roster→repository is direct invocation. (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/internal/VetEventListener.java:24-44`, `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/internal/VetRoster.java:61-73`)
